key_insight: Blackjack uses two similarity-based features from cell-free DNA fragmentation patterns to distinguish cancer from healthy samples, including early-stage cancers.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support minimally invasive multi-cancer detection through blood testing, but clinical screening utility remains unproven.
method: Encode DNA sequence context around fragmentation sites in a position probability matrix.
Measure similarity to matrices from healthy and cancer reference cohorts.
Use the two similarity features in logistic regression.
evidence_signal: Cross-validation on two external whole-genome sequencing datasets yielded a minimum AUC of 0.993 and sensitivity of 91.8% at 98% specificity; stage I sensitivity was 89.8%.
watch_item: Cross-validation results require prospective validation in representative screening populations to establish real-world performance.
paper_title: Detection of early-stage cancer using similarity-based classification of cell-free DNA fragmentation patterns
